attempt: Stochastic cohort, to test whether the threshold model reproduces the SOD1-G93A copy-number series (25 copies fully penetrant at 4.3 months, 8-10 copies fully penetrant at 5.5-7.8 months, 4 copies with ~20 % of animals symptom-free past 24 months).
outcome: IT DOES NOT, and the reason is worth more than the fit would have been.
why: Dose mapped to production gives a cytoplasmic pool that rises only 3x for a 25x increase in production: 0.384 to 1.185. Templated growth kg.C reaches 0.047 against a clearance slope Vmax/Km of 0.150, so there is no runaway at any dose tested. Autoregulation absorbs the dose -- which is the loop doing exactly what it exists to do.
two_honest_reasons: The G93A transgene is NOT autoregulated. It is a foreign gene carrying no TDP-43 feedback, so the buffering this model applies to dose does not apply to it. Simulating a transgene would need an unregulated second species, not a larger p0.

The mouse is a SOD1 model and this is a TDP-43 model. The copy-number series tests dosage of a different protein with a different aggregation mechanism. The structural claim -- that incomplete penetrance at a fixed dose is a threshold signature -- still stands, but it is generic to bistable systems and this simulation does not demonstrate it for these data.
what_was_learned: TDP-43 autoregulation is protective against its own overdosage. A 25-fold increase in production buys a 3-fold increase in the cytoplasmic pool and does not approach the threshold. That is a testable prediction in its own right and it matches something known: TARDBP duplication is not a common cause of ALS, and TDP-43 overexpression models are notoriously hard to interpret because the toxicity tracks the overexpression rather than the disease. A protein that regulates its own level is hard to make pathogenic by raising its level. SOD1, which has no such loop, is easy -- which is why the mouse field runs on SOD1.
two_numerical_failures_recorded: First integration used one timestep for the whole system. Rate constants of 6 per hour against a 2 h step made Euler unstable; everything overflowed and every animal crossed at t=0. Fixed by separating timescales: transport and turnover equilibrate in hours and are slaved to the aggregate, which moves over months.

Second attempt mapped dose to the nucleation constant. Nothing crossed at any dose up to 40x, correctly -- multiplying nucleation raises the flux but barely moves the cytoplasmic pool, and the pool is what drives templating.
status: Negative. Recorded because a model that will not reproduce a target without being bent is more informative than one that has been bent.
